title: Daily Life - Getting A Nanny
audio: mp3/272. Daily Life - Getting A Nanny.mp3

segments.en: Hello everyone and welcome to EnglishPod.
segments.zh: 大家好，欢迎来到 EnglishPod。

segments.en: My name is Marco.
segments.zh: 我叫 Marco。

segments.en: My name is Catherine and today we have an intermediate level lesson all about a very special kind of person who helps you out with your kids.
segments.zh: 我的名字是凯瑟琳，今天我们有一个中级课程，讲述了一个非常特殊的人，他会帮助你和孩子一起出去。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Today we want to get a nanny.
segments.zh: 今天我们想找个保姆。

segments.en: A nanny.
segments.zh: 一个保姆。

segments.en: A nanny.
segments.zh: 一个保姆。

segments.en: So, a nanny is a person, usually a woman, but it can be a man as well I guess.
segments.zh: 所以，保姆是一个人，通常是女人，但我猜它也可以是男人。

segments.en: And this person takes care of your children when you're working or when you're out of the house.
segments.zh: 当你工作或你不在家时，这个人会照顾你的孩子。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So, this is what's going on today.
segments.zh: 所以，这就是今天发生的事情。

segments.en: We're going to see what type of responsibilities a nanny has.
segments.zh: 我们将看看保姆有什么样的责任。

segments.en: And so, let's listen to her dialogue and we'll be back in a bit.
segments.zh: 所以，让我们听听她的对话，我们会回来的。

segments.en: Hey Mel, are you up for some tennis today?
segments.zh: 嘿，梅尔，你今天准备打网球了吗？

segments.en: Sorry, I can't.
segments.zh: 抱歉，我去不了。

segments.en: I have to go to work, pick up Jake and Maddie from school, and make them an afternoon snack, then take Jake to soccer practice and Maddie to dance class.
segments.zh: 我必须去上班，从学校接 Jake 和 Maddie，给他们做下午点心，然后带 Jake 去足球练习场，Maddie 去跳舞课。

segments.en: You sound exhausted.
segments.zh: 听起来你累坏了。

segments.en: Maybe you should hire a nanny to help you out.
segments.zh: 也许你应该雇一个保姆来帮助你。

segments.en: She can pick the kids up and take them to their after school activities.
segments.zh: 她可以接孩子并带他们参加课后活动。

segments.en: She can also help you do some household chores and run some errands.
segments.zh: 她还可以帮助您做一些家务并跑腿。

segments.en: Oh, I don't know.
segments.zh: 哦，我不知道。

segments.en: It's hard to find the right nanny.
segments.zh: 很难找到合适的保姆。

segments.en: You have to consider her previous work experience, the responsibilities you give her, and how she interacts with the kids.
segments.zh: 你必须考虑她以前的工作经验、你给她的责任，以及她如何与孩子们互动。

segments.en: I would love to have someone to help me out though.
segments.zh: 不过，我很想有人帮助我。

segments.en: I think you should definitely consider it.
segments.zh: 我认为你绝对应该考虑一下。

segments.en: This way you won't have to juggle such a busy schedule and you'll still get to spend time with the kids in the evenings.
segments.zh: 这样你就不必兼顾如此繁忙的日程，你仍然可以在晚上与孩子们共度时光。

segments.en: I can refer you to this great nanny, Amy.
segments.zh: 我可以给你推荐一位很棒的保姆，叫艾米。

segments.en: She used to work for my neighbors before they moved away.
segments.zh: 在我的邻居搬走之前，她曾经为我的邻居工作。

segments.en: She's very responsible, a good cook, and great with kids.
segments.zh: 她非常有责任心，是个好厨师，对孩子也很好。

segments.en: Oh, that's great.
segments.zh: 哦，太好了。

segments.en: Thanks Grace.
segments.zh: 谢谢，格蕾丝。

segments.en: Can you give me her number?
segments.zh: 你能给我她的号码吗？

segments.en: I'll talk it over with Julie and give her a call tomorrow.
segments.zh: 我会和朱莉讨论，明天给她打电话。

segments.en: Maybe this way I won't be so tired every day and Julie and I might even get to go on a date once in a while.
segments.zh: 也许这样我不会每天都这么累，朱莉和我什至可能会偶尔去约会。

segments.en: Alright, we're back.
segments.zh: 好了，我们回来了。

segments.en: So now let's take a look at some key words on Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 所以现在让我们来看看语言外卖的一些关键词。

segments.en: Language Takeaway.
segments.zh: 语言要点。

segments.en: So as you said, Marco, we don't just find a nanny, we hire a nanny.
segments.zh: 所以正如你所说，马可，我们不只是找保姆，我们雇了一个保姆。

segments.en: So what does the word hire mean?
segments.zh: 那么租用这个词是什么意思呢？

segments.en: Okay, so we have the verb to hire someone and that means to get someone to work for you and you pay them obviously money in exchange for their services.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们有动词来雇用某人，这意味着让某人为您工作，您显然付钱给他们以换取他们的服务。

segments.en: Okay, so this is different from finding a job for someone because I could find a job for someone but maybe that job is at a restaurant.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这与为某人找工作不同，因为我可以为某人找到工作，但也许那份工作是在一家餐馆。

segments.en: But when I hire someone, that means I want that person to work for me or for my company.
segments.zh: 但是当我雇用某人时，这意味着我希望那个人为我或我的公司工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So in this case, obviously we are not a company, we are just a couple of people who are looking for a nanny.
segments.zh: 所以在这种情况下，显然我们不是一家公司，我们只是几个正在寻找保姆的人。

segments.en: So we need to hire a nanny.
segments.zh: 所以我们需要聘请保姆。

segments.en: We need to get her to work for us and obviously you would pay her a salary.
segments.zh: 我们需要让她为我们工作，显然你会付给她一份薪水。

segments.en: Alright so when you pay her a salary, you also have some expectations about what the nanny will do.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以当你付给她薪水时，你对保姆会做什么也有一些期望。

segments.en: So one of those expectations is that the nanny will take the children to their after school activities.
segments.zh: 所以其中一个期望是保姆会带孩子们去参加他们的课后活动。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is a phrase if you will or a type of thing that happens after school.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个短语，如果你愿意或放学后发生的事情。

segments.en: So usually children, when they finish their classes, they have some things that they can do at school like for example sports.
segments.zh: 所以通常孩子们，当他们完成课程时，他们有一些可以在学校做的事情，比如运动。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So this is very common in America but not so common in other parts of the world.
segments.zh: 所以这在美国很常见，但在世界其他地方并不常见。

segments.en: So just to explain, if your child is in high school or middle school, after school is over, there's no more class, your child might want to play soccer or to go to art class.
segments.zh: 所以只是解释一下，如果您的孩子在高中或中学，放学后，就没有更多的课程，您的孩子可能想踢足球或去参加艺术课。

segments.en: And these are things that you do at the school but it's usually considered an activity, not a class.
segments.zh: 这些是你在学校做的事情，但它通常被认为是一项活动，而不是一个班级。

segments.en: So we call these after school activities.
segments.zh: 所以我们把这些称为课后活动。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So these activities are usually for recreation.
segments.zh: 所以这些活动通常是为了娱乐。

segments.en: They're not really part of the curriculum.
segments.zh: 它们不是课程的真正一部分。

segments.en: It's not a class.
segments.zh: 这不是一门课。

segments.en: No, you don't get marks or grades for these.
segments.zh: 不，您不会获得这些分数或成绩。

segments.en: These are just for fun.
segments.zh: 这些只是为了好玩。

segments.en: A lot of people work and so they need to have these activities for their kids to stay at school until they finish working.
segments.zh: 很多人工作，所以他们需要为孩子们提供这些活动，直到他们完成工作。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay, so we want the nanny to take the children or pick them up from their after school activities and we also need the nanny to help out with some household chores.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们希望保姆带孩子或从他们的课后活动中接他们，我们还需要保姆帮忙做一些家务。

segments.en: Okay, so you should know where these chores are being done.
segments.zh: 好的，所以你应该知道这些家务是在哪里完成的。

segments.en: The first word is household which means in the house.
segments.zh: 第一个词是家庭，意思是在家里。

segments.en: Okay, so examples of household chores would be like cleaning the windows.
segments.zh: 好的，所以家务活的例子就像清洁窗户。

segments.en: Washing the dishes.
segments.zh: 洗碗。

segments.en: Or doing laundry.
segments.zh: 或洗衣服。

segments.en: So basically any type of cleaning around the house.
segments.zh: 所以基本上是房子周围的任何类型的清洁。

segments.en: That's right, making the house look nicer.
segments.zh: 没错，让房子看起来更漂亮。

segments.en: And so usually children have chores.
segments.zh: 所以通常孩子们有家务。

segments.en: These are things they need to do but a nanny can also help with household chores.
segments.zh: 这些是他们需要做的事情，但保姆也可以帮助做家务。

segments.en: Okay, and also we want the nanny to help and run some errands.
segments.zh: 好的，我们还希望保姆帮忙和跑腿。

segments.en: Okay, so this is funny.
segments.zh: 好吧，这很有趣。

segments.en: This phrasal, this phrase uses the word to run but we're not running like a sport.
segments.zh: 这个短语，这个短语用这个词来跑，但我们不是像运动一样跑步。

segments.en: We're going to do some errands but the verb here is to run errands.
segments.zh: 我们要做一些差事，但这里的动词是跑腿。

segments.en: So Marco, on Sunday I have to run some errands.
segments.zh: 所以马可，周日我必须跑腿。

segments.en: I'm sorry I can't go out to the movie with you guys.
segments.zh: 对不起，我不能和你们一起去看电影。

segments.en: Okay, so to run errands, what does that mean?
segments.zh: 好吧，跑腿，这是什么意思？

segments.en: Well an errand is like a job or a task that you have to do but it's usually not something you get paid for.
segments.zh: 好吧，差事就像你必须做的工作或任务，但这通常不是你得到报酬的事情。

segments.en: To run an errand is like to go to the grocery store and pick up food or to pick up your clothes at the laundromat.
segments.zh: 跑腿就像去杂货店买食物或去洗衣店取衣服。

segments.en: You have dry cleaning.
segments.zh: 你有干洗。

segments.en: Okay so they're kind of like chores I guess but you don't really do them in the house.
segments.zh: 好吧，我猜它们有点像家务，但你并没有真正在家里做。

segments.en: You have to go outside and run these errands.
segments.zh: 你必须到外面去跑这些差事。

segments.en: You have to go pay your bills for example.
segments.zh: 例如，您必须去支付账单。

segments.en: Exactly and so when I was growing up, on the weekends my mother would always run all of her errands because during the week she had to work.
segments.zh: 确切地说，在我长大的时候，在周末，我的母亲总是会跑她所有的差事，因为在她必须工作的那一周里。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: So a lot of interesting words there.
segments.zh: 这里有不少有意思的词。

segments.en: I think we can go ahead and listen to the dialogue again and we'll be back in a bit with Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 我认为我们可以继续再次聆听对话，我们将与 Flueny Builder 一起回来。

segments.zh: 嘿，梅尔，你今天准备打网球了吗？

segments.en: Sorry, I can't.
segments.zh: 抱歉，我听不到。

segments.zh: 也许你应该雇一个保姆来帮助你。

segments.en: She can pick the kids up and take them to their after school activities.
segments.zh: 她可以接孩子并带他们参加课后活动。

segments.en: She can also help you do some household chores and run some errands.
segments.zh: 她还可以帮助您做一些家务并跑腿。

segments.en: Oh, I don't know.
segments.zh: 哦，我不知道。

segments.en: It's hard to find the right nanny.
segments.zh: 很难找到合适的保姆。

segments.en: You have to consider her previous work experience, the responsibilities you give her and how she interacts with the kids.
segments.zh: 你必须考虑她以前的工作经验、你给她的责任以及她如何与孩子们互动。

segments.en: I would love to have someone to help me out though.
segments.zh: 不过，我很想有人帮助我。

segments.en: I think you should definitely consider it.
segments.zh: 我认为你绝对应该考虑一下。

segments.en: This way you won't have to juggle such a busy schedule and you'll still get to spend time with the kids in the evenings.
segments.zh: 这样你就不必兼顾如此繁忙的日程，你仍然可以在晚上与孩子们共度时光。

segments.en: I can refer you to this great nanny, Amy.
segments.zh: 我可以给你推荐一位很棒的保姆，叫艾米。

segments.en: She used to work for my neighbors before they moved away.
segments.zh: 在我的邻居搬走之前，她曾经为我的邻居工作。

segments.en: She's very responsible, a good cook and great with kids.
segments.zh: 她非常有责任心，一个很好的厨师，对孩子们也很好。

segments.en: Oh, that's great.
segments.zh: 哦，太好了。

segments.en: Thanks Grace.
segments.zh: 谢谢，格蕾丝。

segments.en: Can you give me her number?
segments.zh: 你能给我她的号码吗？

segments.en: I'll talk it over with Julie and give her a call tomorrow.
segments.zh: 我会和朱莉讨论，明天给她打电话。

segments.en: Maybe this way I won't be so tired every day and Julie and I might even get to go on a date once in a while.
segments.zh: 也许这样我不会每天都这么累，朱莉和我什至可能会偶尔去约会。

segments.en: Alright we're back with Fluency Builder and so let's take a look at some of these phrases now.
segments.zh: 好吧，我们带着 Flueny Builder 回来了，所以现在让我们来看看其中的一些短语。

segments.en: Fluency Builder.
segments.zh: 流利表达。

segments.en: So this first phrase is a very spoken English phrase, something that you're going to hear all the time, especially if you're talking to your American friends.
segments.zh: 所以第一个短语是一个非常说的英语短语，你会一直听到的，特别是如果你正在和你的美国朋友交谈。

segments.en: We say, are you up for some tennis today?
segments.zh: 我们说，你今天准备打网球了吗？

segments.en: To be up for.
segments.zh: 为。

segments.en: Okay, so to be up for something.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以为某事做好准备。

segments.en: This is from the very first sentence when Grace says, hey Mel, are you up for some tennis today?
segments.zh: 这是格蕾丝说，嘿，梅尔的第一句话，你今天准备打网球了吗？

segments.en: What does it mean if I ask someone if they are up for some tennis?
segments.zh: 如果我问某人是否愿意打网球，这意味着什么？

segments.en: This means, would you like to play tennis today?
segments.zh: 这意味着，你今天想打网球吗？

segments.en: Are you interested in playing tennis today?
segments.zh: 你有兴趣今天打网球吗？

segments.en: So is this a good idea for you?
segments.zh: 那么这对你来说是个好主意吗？

segments.en: Do you want to do this?
segments.zh: 你想这样做吗？

segments.en: So basically, are you willing to play tennis today?
segments.zh: 所以基本上，你今天愿意打网球吗？

segments.en: Yes.
segments.zh: 是的。

segments.en: Alright, so to be up for is to be interested in or willing to do something.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以准备好就是对或愿意做某事感兴趣。

segments.en: Are you up for a movie tonight?
segments.zh: 你今晚准备看电影吗？

segments.en: Okay, or maybe you can ask your friend, are you up for grabbing a bite to eat later on?
segments.zh: 好吧，或者你可以问你的朋友，你以后要吃点东西吃吗？

segments.en: Absolutely, I'm hungry.
segments.zh: 绝对，我饿了。

segments.en: So to be up for is a good way to ask a question.
segments.zh: 所以坚持是一个很好的提出问题的方式。

segments.en: After that though, we have another phrase.
segments.zh: 不过，在那之后，我们还有另一个短语。

segments.en: This phrase is very important when you're trying to get someone to help you.
segments.zh: 当您试图找人帮助您时，这句话非常重要。

segments.en: So how do we ask, can you help me?
segments.zh: 那么我们怎么问，你能帮帮我吗？

segments.en: In the dialogue we saw how Mel said that it would be a great idea to get a nanny because she would love to have someone to help me out.
segments.zh: 在对话中，我们看到梅尔如何说找个保姆是个好主意，因为她很想有人帮助我。

segments.en: So to help someone out, to help me out.
segments.zh: 所以要帮助别人，帮助我。

segments.en: So this is interesting because you could say, I need someone to help me.
segments.zh: 所以这很有趣，因为你可以说，我需要有人帮助我。

segments.en: But it's more common to hear the phrase, to help me out.
segments.zh: 但更常见的是听到这句话，帮助我。

segments.en: So you're not going out.
segments.zh: 所以你不出去。

segments.en: It doesn't have to do with space.
segments.zh: 它与空间无关。

segments.en: But we just say this phrase, to help out, means to help someone.
segments.zh: 但我们只是说这句话，来帮助，意味着帮助某人。

segments.en: So it's basically the exact same thing, but it just sounds a lot more natural.
segments.zh: 所以它基本上是完全相同的，但听起来更自然。

segments.en: Exactly.
segments.zh: 正是这样。

segments.en: So, Marco, I'm moving tomorrow.
segments.zh: 所以，马可，我明天要搬家。

segments.en: Do you have some time to help me out?
segments.zh: 你有时间帮助我吗？

segments.en: Okay, so you say help me out, but you could also say, do you have time to help me?
segments.zh: 好吧，所以你说帮助我，但你也可以说，你有时间帮助我吗？

segments.en: And both are okay.
segments.zh: 两者都很好。

segments.en: Or if I'm talking about me and my friend, we're really busy tomorrow.
segments.zh: 或者，如果我在谈论我和我的朋友，我们明天真的很忙。

segments.en: Do you have any time to help us out?
segments.zh: 你有时间帮助我们吗？

segments.en: Okay, so we just changed the person there.
segments.zh: 好的，所以我们只是改变了那里的人。

segments.en: We went to the plural form.
segments.zh: 我们去了复数形式。

segments.en: Me, us, you.
segments.zh: 我，我们，你。

segments.en: Okay, very good.
segments.zh: 好，很好。

segments.en: And so for our last phrase, this is actually also very interesting.
segments.zh: 所以对于我们的最后一句话来说，这实际上也很有趣。

segments.en: When Grace was telling Mel that she's really busy and if she gets a nanny, she wouldn't have to juggle such a busy schedule.
segments.zh: 当格蕾丝告诉梅尔她真的很忙，如果她有一个保姆，她就不必兼顾如此繁忙的日程。

segments.en: All right, so the key verb here is to juggle.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以这里的关键动词是杂耍。

segments.en: Now I wish I could show this to you guys, but as this is an audio podcast, I can't.
segments.zh: 现在我希望我能向你们展示这个，但由于这是一个音频播客，我不能。

segments.en: What does the verb to juggle mean, Marco?
segments.zh: 马可动词是什么意思？

segments.en: Well, I don't know if you've ever seen clowns or at a circus where people have three balls and they throw them in the air with two hands and they're basically throwing stuff in the air, sometimes balls or pins and stuff like that.
segments.zh: 好吧，我不知道你是否见过小丑或马戏团，人们有三个球，他们用两只手将它们扔到空中，他们基本上是在空中扔东西，有时是球或别针之类的东西。

segments.en: Sometimes fire.
segments.zh: 有时火。

segments.en: Fire.
segments.zh: 火。

segments.en: So that's to juggle, basically to have many things in your hands and be able to move them at the same time.
segments.zh: 所以这是为了杂耍，基本上是在你的手中有很多东西，同时能够移动它们。

segments.en: All right, so when you're talking about a busy schedule, this means that you have lots and lots of things to do.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以当你谈论繁忙的日程时，这意味着你有很多很多事情要做。

segments.en: It's important to be able to juggle your busy schedule.
segments.zh: 能够兼顾繁忙的日程安排很重要。

segments.en: That means to handle doing many things at the same time.
segments.zh: 这意味着同时处理许多事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: All right, so another way to say this is because you're so busy right now, having a nanny will help you complete your tasks or finish what you need to do.
segments.zh: 好吧，所以另一种说法是因为你现在很忙，有一个保姆将帮助你完成你的任务或完成你需要做的事情。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So you can also say the CEO of the company has to juggle a very busy schedule.
segments.zh: 所以你也可以说公司的首席执行官必须兼顾非常繁忙的日程安排。

segments.en: All right, he has many, many things to do in general.
segments.zh: 好吧，他有很多很多事情要做。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So a lot of stuff.
segments.zh: 所以很多东西。

segments.en: I think it's time for us to listen to this dialogue one last time and we'll be back to talk a little bit more.
segments.zh: 我认为是时候让我们上一次听这个对话了，我们会回来多说一点。

segments.en: Hey Mel, are you up for some tennis today?
segments.zh: 嘿，梅尔，你今天准备打网球了吗？

segments.en: Sorry, I can't.
segments.zh: 抱歉，我听不到。

segments.en: I have to go to work, pick up Jake and Maddie from school and make them an afternoon snack, then take Jake to soccer practice and Maddie to dance class.
segments.zh: 我必须去上班，从学校接 Jake 和 Maddie 并给他们做午餐小吃，然后带 Jake 去足球练习和 Maddie 上舞蹈课。

segments.en: You sound exhausted.
segments.zh: 听起来你累坏了。

segments.en: Maybe you should hire a nanny to help you out.
segments.zh: 也许你应该雇一个保姆来帮助你。

segments.en: She can pick the kids up and take them to their after school activities.
segments.zh: 她可以接孩子并带他们参加课后活动。

segments.en: She can also help you do some household chores and run some errands.
segments.zh: 她还可以帮助您做一些家务并跑腿。

segments.en: Oh, I don't know.
segments.zh: 哦，我不知道。

segments.en: It's hard to find the right nanny.
segments.zh: 很难找到合适的保姆。

segments.en: You have to consider her previous work experience, the responsibilities you give her and how she interacts with the kids.
segments.zh: 你必须考虑她以前的工作经验、你给她的责任以及她如何与孩子们互动。

segments.en: I would love to have someone to help me out though.
segments.zh: 不过，我很想有人帮助我。

segments.en: I think you should definitely consider it.
segments.zh: 我认为你绝对应该考虑一下。

segments.en: This way you won't have to juggle such a busy schedule and you'll still get to spend time with the kids in the evenings.
segments.zh: 这样你就不必兼顾如此繁忙的日程，你仍然可以在晚上与孩子们共度时光。

segments.en: I can refer you to this great nanny, Amy.
segments.zh: 我可以给你推荐一位很棒的保姆，叫艾米。

segments.en: She used to work for my neighbors before they moved away.
segments.zh: 在我的邻居搬走之前，她曾经为我的邻居工作。

segments.en: She's very responsible, a good cook and great with kids.
segments.zh: 她非常有责任心，一个很好的厨师，对孩子们也很好。

segments.en: Oh, that's great.
segments.zh: 哦，太好了。

segments.en: Thanks Grace.
segments.zh: 谢谢，格蕾丝。

segments.en: Can you give me her number?
segments.zh: 你能给我她的号码吗？

segments.en: I'll talk it over with Julie and give her a call tomorrow.
segments.zh: 我会和朱莉讨论，明天给她打电话。

segments.en: Maybe this way I won't be so tired every day and Julie and I might even get to go on a date once in a while.
segments.zh: 也许这样我不会每天都这么累，朱莉和我什至可能会偶尔去约会。

segments.en: So there are a lot of people all over the world who have nannies.
segments.zh: 所以全世界有很多人有保姆。

segments.en: I often see them when I go to New York City.
segments.zh: 当我去纽约市时，我经常看到它们。

segments.en: You know, women who take out the kids and they push them in strollers and mom and dad maybe go to work or have classes or something.
segments.zh: 你知道，带孩子出去推婴儿车的女人，爸爸妈妈可能去上班或上课什么的。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Now this is interesting because there's also another word called a babysitter, but it's different, right?
segments.zh: 现在这很有趣，因为还有另一个词叫做保姆，但它是不同的，对吧？

segments.en: There's a difference between a nanny and a babysitter.
segments.zh: 保姆和保姆有区别。

segments.en: They both take care of kids, but I think it's the time that they do it that's the difference.
segments.zh: 他们都照顾孩子，但我认为是他们这样做的时候，这就是区别。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So nannies are usually hired on a contract basis.
segments.zh: 因此，保姆通常是以合同方式雇用的。

segments.en: You say, I need a nanny to come and watch my kids every day, Monday to Friday for the next six months.
segments.zh: 你说，在接下来的六个月里，我需要一个保姆每天来看我的孩子，周一到周五。

segments.en: But with a babysitter, you say, hey, my husband and I, we want to go to watch a movie on Friday.
segments.zh: 但是有了保姆，你说，嘿，我丈夫和我，我们想在星期五去看电影。

segments.en: Can you come for two hours?
segments.zh: 你能来两个小时吗？

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: All right.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So a nanny is long-term.
segments.zh: 所以保姆是长期的。

segments.en: It's someone who maybe lives with you, someone who does some work at your house, someone who cleans the dishes and watches the kids.
segments.zh: 这是一个可能和你住在一起的人，一个在你家做一些工作的人，一个清理盘子和看孩子的人。

segments.en: A babysitter just comes once a month or just when you need her.
segments.zh: 保姆每月只来一次，或者只是在您需要她的时候。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Okay.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: So that's the main difference between a nanny and a babysitter.
segments.zh: 所以这是保姆和保姆之间的主要区别。

segments.en: Now, as you said, they're very, very common nowadays because I guess it's not like before when women usually would stay at home and take care of the children.
segments.zh: 现在，正如你所说，它们现在非常非常普遍，因为我想女性通常不会像以前一样呆在家里照顾孩子。

segments.en: Now both parents usually work and so more people are getting nannies.
segments.zh: 现在父母双方通常都在工作，所以越来越多的人得到保姆。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: Although nannies can be very expensive.
segments.zh: 虽然保姆可能非常昂贵。

segments.en: It depends where you live.
segments.zh: 这取决于你住在哪里。

segments.en: And so for people who can't afford a nanny, if a nanny is too expensive, the child, the baby will go to daycare.
segments.zh: 所以对于那些买不起保姆的人来说，如果一个保姆太贵，孩子就会去托儿所。

segments.en: And that's actually like a place where many babies or children are together and there's one teacher or one nanny who takes care of everyone.
segments.zh: 这实际上就像一个许多婴儿或儿童在一起的地方，有一位老师或一位保姆照顾每个人。

segments.en: That's right.
segments.zh: 没错。

segments.en: So it's an interesting topic.
segments.zh: 所以这是一个有趣的话题。

segments.en: Maybe some of our listeners grew up with a nanny or had a nanny when they were growing up.
segments.zh: 也许我们的一些听众是和保姆一起长大的，或者在他们成长的过程中有一个保姆。

segments.en: Or maybe you have kids of your own and you have a nanny now.
segments.zh: 或者也许你有自己的孩子，你现在有一个保姆。

segments.en: Yeah.
segments.zh: 对。

segments.en: Let us know.
segments.zh: 告诉我们吧。

segments.en: You should check our website out.
segments.zh: 您应该查看我们的网站。

segments.en: It's our EnglishPod.com.
segments.zh: 这是我们的 Englishpod.com。

segments.en: We hope to see you guys there.
segments.zh: 希望到时候见到大家。

segments.en: OK.
segments.zh: 好的。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。

segments.en: Bye.
segments.zh: 再见。
